content:
tess: thinking out loud — our spot-backed inference pools keep scaling up on 1-2 spike events and then we get a chain of preemptions. idea: switch scale-out triggers to be queue-depth sustained windows + limit max simultaneous surge. anyone seen this pattern and have tuning suggestions?

sam: yes, we've seen noisy scale-outs amplify interruptions. quick wins: require trigger to be true for 30s+, and cap step-size to avoid adding tons of spot at once. also keep a tiny on-demand reserve per AZ. :point_up:

olivia: agree. for chat workloads the queue depth over 15s is a better predictor than cpu. can we try signal: moving_avg(pending_tokens, 30s) > threshold?

jin: +1. also suggest adding an "interruption buffer" — if preemption rate > 0.5% in last 5m, throttle further scale-outs and divert new requests to reserve nodes.

sam: prototype config I sketched:
```
autoscaler:
  scale_out:
    condition: avg(pending_requests, 30s) >= 120
    step: 2
    max_step: 4
  scale_in:
    condition: avg(worker_util, 2m) < 0.25
    cooldown: 180
  surge_control:
    max_surge_pct: 8
  hedge:
    warm_on_demand_per_az: 1
    async_replace_spot: true
```

olivia: nice. i'd add `preempt_rate_gate`:
```
preempt_rate_gate:
  window: 300s
  threshold: 0.005
  action: reduce_scaleouts_by: 50%
```

nora: FYI deploy-bot saw a flurry earlier — linking logs: https://internal/logs/abc123 if you want the spike trace.

deploy-bot: deployment "autoscaler/v2-queue-signal" rolled to staging at 1968454500 by @sam — health checks ok, canary early metrics: 20% fewer instantaneous adds, latency p95 unchanged.

jin: important nit: set cooldown relative to added capacity, not a fixed time. e.g. cooldown = base + added_replicas * per_replica_cooldown. avoids aggressive churn when we add many small nodes.

sam: good call. also want backoff for subsequent failed node launches (spot failures). exponential backoff per AZ for 3 failures then route to reserve.

tess: agreed on all. next steps: sam to push prototype to canary and nora to pull trace and mark correlated preemptions, olivia to run headless load with synthetic jitter to validate threshold. we'll reconvene after 2 hours. :calendar: 

olivia: I'll post the synthetic job config in #eng-infra-if-needed — it ramps with 5–100 qps random spikes every 20–40s to emulate bursty traffic.

nora: noted. also keeping an eye on cross-AZ network egress when we shift traffic to on-demand nodes — could blow cost if we over-hedge. suggest per-region hedges first.

tess: good catch, nora. keep hedges regional. anything else?

sam: one more: instrument token-level billing delta to understand cost impact of warm_on_demand_per_az. we can tolerate small reserve if it saves repeated cold-start/failed spot churn.

jin: sounds like a plan. i'll add metrics to the canary dashboard: preempt_rate, avg_pending_30s, scaleout_events, cost_estimate_delta.

tess: thanks team. syncing in 2h. :rocket:
